text: {"overall_winner":"B","qualities":[{"evidence":"clear claim that driverless cars \"aren't practical\"","quality":"argumentative focus","description":"It states a direct position early and keeps returning to the same central claim throughout the essay."},{"evidence":"explains drivers must stay alert, laws must change, and liability is unclear","quality":"reasoning development","description":"It develops multiple linked reasons that explain why the position is true rather than just asserting it."},{"evidence":"uses rhetorical questions and a hypothetical sixty-car pile-up","quality":"elaboration","description":"It extends points with concrete scenarios and audience-facing questions that make the argument feel more fully worked out."},{"evidence":"repeats the idea that the cars are \"not practical\" in different paragraphs","quality":"cohesion","description":"It maintains a unified line of argument with transitions that keep the essay organized around one main idea."},{"evidence":"concludes that efforts \"will be in vain\"","quality":"conclusion strength","description":"It ends by restating the position decisively and wrapping the argument up rather than stopping abruptly."}]}
